title: From git push to production on EKS
summary: My 2024 Jenkins-to-EKS pipeline rebuilt with GitHub Actions, signed images, Argo CD GitOps, canary releases and full observability.
problem: The 2024 pipeline worked end to end, but the cluster was created by hand with eksctl, Jenkins pushed images straight into the cluster, and nothing checked an image before it ran.
solution: Terraform builds all infrastructure. GitHub Actions connects to AWS with OIDC and runs Gitleaks, SonarQube and Trivy before signing the image with Cosign and pushing it to ECR. Argo CD deploys from a GitOps repo, Kyverno only admits signed images, and Argo Rollouts releases in canary steps. OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo and Grafana cover observability.
outcome: Design complete and build under way. Every release will be scanned, signed and rolled out gradually with automatic rollback.

title: Security scanning built into GitHub Actions
summary: SonarQube, Snyk and AWS Inspector run on every pipeline across Java, .NET and Python services.
problem: Code security issues across several language stacks needed to be caught in the pipeline, with policies enforced automatically rather than by manual review.
solution: Integrated SonarQube, Snyk and AWS Inspector into GitHub Actions pipelines for real-time vulnerability scanning and automated policy enforcement across Java, .NET and Python.
outcome: A reduction of more than 30% in code security issues across multiple language stacks.

title: CI/CD for containerised microservices
summary: Pipelines that build, test, store artifacts and deploy Docker microservices to Kubernetes.
problem: Building, testing and deploying microservices took heavy manual effort and slowed delivery.
solution: Designed scalable CI/CD pipelines using AWS DevOps, Jenkins and GitLab CI/CD to automate build, test, artifact management and deployment of Docker microservices orchestrated by Kubernetes.
outcome: 70% less manual deployment effort and 40–50% faster delivery cycles.

title: AWS cost optimisation without losing availability
summary: Auto scaling, cost tagging and budget monitoring across EC2, ECS, EKS, Fargate and Lambda.
problem: Cloud spend needed to come down without putting availability or SLA compliance at risk.
solution: Optimised and supported EC2, API Gateway, S3, ECS, EKS, Fargate, Lambda, WAF, Route 53 and CloudTrail, using Auto Scaling groups, cost tagging and budget monitoring tools.
outcome: A 30% reduction in cloud spend with no impact on application availability or SLA compliance.

title: Centralised monitoring and observability
summary: Logstash, Kibana, CloudWatch and Datadog in one monitoring picture.
problem: Incidents took too long to detect and diagnose across distributed services.
solution: Built centralised monitoring and observability with Logstash and Kibana alongside AWS CloudWatch and Datadog.
outcome: 99.99% uptime maintained, faster incident detection, and root cause analysis 45% faster.

title: Hybrid infrastructure with Terraform and Ansible
summary: Automated provisioning of compute, networking and storage across hybrid environments.
problem: Environments built by hand drifted apart across on-premise and AWS.
solution: Engineered resilient infrastructure with Terraform and Ansible, automating provisioning of compute, networking and storage across hybrid environments on AWS.
outcome: Consistent, cross-platform environments with parity between them.

title: Legacy services modernised onto OpenShift
summary: Containerised legacy services with reusable Dockerfiles, Helm and GitOps workflows.
problem: Legacy services were hard to deploy consistently and images were not standardised.
solution: Containerised legacy services into Docker and deployed them to OpenShift and Kubernetes, with reusable Dockerfiles, Helm charts, managed image repositories and GitOps workflows on GitLab and GitHub. Kubernetes RBAC applied with the cybersecurity team.
outcome: Standardised deployments, better image hygiene and streamlined development workflows.

title: Bash and Python operations automation
summary: Container lifecycle, log parsing, SSL certificate rotation and compliance validation.
problem: Repetitive operational tasks created overhead and let configuration drift in.
solution: Developed automation frameworks in Bash and Python for container lifecycle management, log parsing, SSL certificate rotation and compliance validation.
outcome: Lower operations overhead and minimal configuration drift.

title: Elasticsearch to OpenSearch migration
summary: Migrated Elasticsearch clusters to OpenSearch on AWS with Kibana dashboards in every environment.
problem: Log analytics clusters had to move to OpenSearch without interrupting applications.
solution: Executed the migration of Elasticsearch clusters to OpenSearch and configured Kibana dashboards across all AWS environments.
outcome: Zero application downtime and better real-time data exploration and log analytics.

title: RHEL 7 to RHEL 8 upgrade
summary: Fleet upgrade orchestrated with Chef and Ansible.
problem: Servers had to move to RHEL 8 to stay within vendor support without service interruption.
solution: Collaborated on the upgrade from RHEL 7 to RHEL 8, orchestrated through Chef and Ansible.
outcome: Zero-downtime migrations, full vendor support compliance, and improved stability and security.

title: Legacy Jenkins pipelines redesigned
summary: Continuous delivery for .NET Core, Java and Node.js microservices on Tomcat and NGINX.
problem: Legacy pipelines involved manual steps that slowed releases and caused errors.
solution: Redesigned and automated CI/CD pipelines in Jenkins for .NET Core, Java and Node.js microservices integrated with Tomcat and NGINX.
outcome: Significantly faster deployments and fewer manual errors.

title: EKS and AWS platform with Terraform
summary: Load balancers, Auto Scaling groups and EKS clusters via Terraform and CloudFormation.
problem: The platform needed to scale and be observable end to end.
solution: Provisioned scalable AWS infrastructure with Terraform and CloudFormation: Elastic Load Balancers, Auto Scaling groups and EKS clusters, integrated with CloudWatch, Datadog and ELK.
outcome: Complete system observability and actionable insight across the platform.

title: Encrypted NGINX ingress on OpenShift
summary: Production-grade ingress with end-to-end encryption for internal microservices.
problem: Internal microservices needed encrypted traffic and less exposure to the outside.
solution: Implemented a secure ingress architecture using NGINX in OpenShift environments with end-to-end encrypted data transmission.
outcome: End-to-end encryption and a minimised external attack surface.

title: Controlled egress with Squid proxies
summary: Squid proxy servers in private AWS subnets for controlled outbound traffic.
problem: Workloads in private subnets needed package access without uncontrolled internet egress.
solution: Deployed Squid proxy servers in AWS private subnets to control outbound traffic and provide secure package access.
outcome: Controlled outbound traffic supporting high-availability deployments.

title: Linux fleet automation for national tax systems
summary: Patching, log rotation, backups and agent rollout scripted for 100+ servers.
problem: 100+ Linux servers behind mission-critical tax and revenue platforms relied on manual maintenance.
solution: Automated patch management, log rotation, backup scheduling and monitoring agent deployment using Bash and Python, with Git-based version control for configs and scripts.
outcome: Manual workload reduced by more than 50%, with 24/7 availability maintained.

title: Proactive server monitoring with Nagios
summary: Nagios plus custom checks for real-time performance and health diagnostics.
problem: Server problems were discovered after they caused outages.
solution: Implemented system monitoring with Nagios and custom scripts for real-time performance checks and proactive health diagnostics.
